statement: Let $P$ be a unary predicate on a set $A$, and let $xs$ and $ys$ be vectors of $A$ of lengths $m$ and $n$ respectively. If every element of $xs$ satisfies $P$ and every element of $ys$ satisfies $P$, then every element of the concatenation $xs \mathbin{++} ys$ satisfies $P$. In other words, $P$ holds pointwise on $xs$ and pointwise on $ys$ implies $P$ holds pointwise on $xs \mathbin{++} ys$; the proof is by splitting an index of the concatenation according to whether it lands in the first $m$ positions (using the corresponding element of $xs$) or in the last $n$ positions (using the corresponding element of $ys$).
